questions.q: What does the `-e` flag in `set -euo pipefail` do?
options: Prints every command before running it
Exits the script immediately if any command returns a non-zero exit code
Encrypts variables stored in the script
Enables extended globbing patterns
questions.explain: `-e` causes the script to exit immediately on any command that returns a non-zero (failure) exit code, instead of continuing on to the next line.

questions.q: Without `pipefail`, what exit code does a pipeline like `cmd1 | cmd2` return if `cmd1` fails but `cmd2` succeeds?
options: The exit code of cmd1
A combined error code made from both commands
The exit code of cmd2 (the last command), even though cmd1 failed
Bash refuses to run the pipeline at all
questions.explain: Without `pipefail`, a pipeline's exit code is only the exit code of its last command, so an earlier failure in the pipe can be silently masked by a later success.

questions.q: Why does `rm $RELEASE_NOTE` behave differently from `rm "$RELEASE_NOTE"` when the variable holds "release notes oct.txt"?
options: There is no difference; quoting is just a style preference
The unquoted version is word-split by bash into three separate arguments
The quoted version runs faster
The unquoted version automatically escapes spaces
questions.explain: An unquoted variable expansion is subject to word-splitting, so a value with spaces becomes multiple separate arguments to `rm` instead of one filename.

questions.q: In Northbridge's deploy script, why is the function registered with `trap cleanup EXIT` guaranteed to run even if an earlier command fails under `set -e`?
options: `trap ... EXIT` runs on any script exit, including the one triggered by set -e catching a failure
It isn't guaranteed; trap only runs on a normal, successful exit
set -e disables all traps automatically
trap only works inside functions, never at the top level of a script
questions.explain: An EXIT trap fires whenever the script exits, for any reason, including an early exit triggered by set -e — which is exactly why it's reliable for cleanup like releasing a lock file.

questions.q: A script returns exit code 0 after a `cp` that actually failed due to a bad path. What's the most likely missing piece?
options: The script needs more comments
`set -euo pipefail` was not set, so the failed `cp` didn't stop the script or affect its final exit code
The shebang line is missing
`cp` never returns a non-zero exit code
questions.explain: Without `set -e`, a failed command doesn't stop the script, and whatever comes after it (like an `echo "success"` and exit 0) determines the final exit code, masking the real failure.
